approvalRule: A frozen reviewReady flag is historical. Apply the later advisory before deciding whether to approve that specific revision. No human approval is recorded.

laterAdvisories.title: An Efficacy Trial of an Intervention Program for Children Exposed to Intimate Partner Violence.

original.finding: ITT analyses found reduced internalizing problems for girls at follow-up; per-protocol analyses favored treatment for boys and girls immediately after treatment.
original.limitation: Benefits varied by analysis and sex; completer effects should not replace the more qualified ITT findings. Masking and attrition are not established here.
original.adverseFindings: Adverse events not established from accessed source; absence of reporting is not absence of harm.

laterAdvisories.newEvidence: The original 2015 paper, publicly posted by a coauthor, describes the first five eligible families at each site receiving intervention and the next five comparison. Authors call allocation random but do not describe a stochastic sequence or randomized starting rule. Its own methods are now accessible; the concern no longer rests solely on the later report.
laterAdvisories.revisedInterpretation: Randomization remains unverified pending reconciliation. Temporarily withhold the verified-RCT cross. This is not a definitive nonrandomized verdict. Original findings remain analysis- and sex-dependent.
laterAdvisories.requiredBeforeApproval: A contemporaneous protocol or allocation schedule must establish the random mechanism and reconcile five-family blocks here with six-family blocks in the follow-up. Do not approve the frozen revision meanwhile.
laterAdvisories.sourceLocation: Original Method / Study Protocol; later report pp. 853–854
